author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: G4/B1: the "Choose something else when" row says "The options change without a new release, like categories kept in a database; load them as data." Database, release and "load them as data" are not taught in Java Foundations (databases come in a later course) and are not explained in a clause, so the learner is not told what to reach for instead.
findings.recommendation: Explain the alternative in a clause using taught ideas, for example "The options can change while the program runs, such as product categories staff can add; keep them as ordinary String values in a list or map instead."

location.selector: #activity-3 #prob-3 (inline engine: parse error for enum constant list)

findings.claim: E1/E5 (policy 1.3): leaving out the semicolon after the constant list ("QUARTER(25)" with no ";") shows "Error, line 4: ',', '}', or ';' expected": the raw parser message is not translated into a next step, and it points at line 4 (the field) instead of line 2, where the semicolon is missing. The teaching says "the constant list ... ends with a semicolon", so this is the error this activity most invites.
findings.recommendation: Translate this message ("The constant list must end with a semicolon: add ; after the last constant") and report the line of the last constant, or say "check the end of the line before line 4".

findings.claim: B1: the objective says "explain the type safety it adds", but "type safety" is never defined; Activity 4 feedback says a switch expression "must be exhaustive" and that "a switch statement with patterns or a null case" must be too. "Exhaustive" and "patterns" are not taught on this page or earlier ones (the teaching says "cover every constant").
findings.recommendation: Write the objective in taught words ("explain how an enum lets the compiler reject wrong values"), say "must cover every constant" in the feedback, and drop the "patterns or a null case" clause or gloss it.

findings.claim: E1/B5: a wrong lane press gives "Not Compiles." or "Not Compiler rejects it." because the verdict prefixes "Not" to the lane label, which reads as broken English.
findings.recommendation: Phrase the wrong-lane verdict as "Not this lane: <lane label>" in the engine wording shared across pages.

findings.claim: A4: the probe "why use an enum instead of int constants?" is exactly what Activity 2 practises, and the page does not say so.
findings.recommendation: Append "Activity 2 practises this." to the In interviews row.

findings.claim: Other real problem (E1/F5): the practice editor does not check statements inside method or constructor bodies. Exercised at 570 px: Coin.java with "this.cents = cents" (missing ";") inside the constructor is accepted. The Problems tab says "No problems found in the parts this editor reads" and feedback says "All 8 checks pass", while other syntax errors on the same page are reported as "the compiler would reject this code". A beginner reads the pass as "this compiles" and learns that the missing semicolon or bracket is fine. Overlaps the SME fidelity review.
findings.recommendation: Either have the parser require a terminating ";" and balanced parentheses on body statements, reporting them through the existing "Not checked ... does not count as a try" path, or state beside Check code that statement punctuation inside methods is not checked, so the pass is not read as "compiles".

location.selector: #activity-3 #fb-3 (inline engine: second checked try, verdict set)

findings.claim: E3 (practice-feedback-policy 1.1): a near-miss is only treated as one on the first checked try ("Almost: ..."). On the second (last) checked try the same one-detail miss leads with the failure verdict "Not this time: N-1 of N checks pass after your second checked try" (observed for a label() switch that adds a default case), and the activity is closed for credit. The policy says a near-miss never gets a failure verdict.
findings.recommendation: When exactly one check fails on the last checked try, lead with the near-miss verdict ("Almost: ...") and the specific nudge, in pep-verdict--near styling, then state that the result is recorded and practice can continue.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion summary names activities by internal labels ("Enum type safety", "Enum with data", "Final check") that match none of the lesson-path row titles the learner has seen ("Let the compiler reject bad values", "Give coins their values in cents", "Predict what a switch does"). A learner told "Enum with data: answered, not yet correct" has to guess which activity that is.
findings.recommendation: Make each PEP_PAGE label equal to its lesson-path row title, or have the completion summary read the row title.

findings.claim: GIFT/B2: the item asks when an enum constructor runs ("Once per constant, when the enum is first set up"); the page says only that "the constants call it", never when, so the keyed answer is inferred rather than retrieved. The o2 public-constructor feedback also asserts "It is private even when you write no modifier", which the page does not teach.
findings.recommendation: Add one teaching clause ("each constant is created once, when the enum is first used") or replace the item with one about passing values to the constructor.

location.selector: h2 "Cheat sheet" and h2 "Static interaction alternatives"

findings.claim: Other real problem (companion): the Markdown companion files every hint, the optional anecdote or challenge text under the "Cheat sheet" heading, repeats the summary text ("Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity 3"), titles the static alternatives with engine type names ("predict", "drag", "explore", "mcq"; the lane activity is not dragged), and omits the On the job card with its At work and In interviews rows. The same generator output appears on all 255 topics, so this is a tooling defect rather than this page's authoring.
findings.recommendation: Raise a tooling-branch fix: give hints, anecdote and challenge their own headings, use activity titles instead of interaction types, de-duplicate summary text and carry the On the job card. No page-level change needed in this module branch.
